source.title: Dynamical Isometry and a Mean Field Theory of CNNs: How to Train 10, 000-Layer Vanilla Convolutional Neural Networks
source.authors: Lechao Xiao; Yasaman Bahri; Jascha Narain Sohl-Dickstein; S. Schoenholz; Jeffrey Pennington

record.file_problem: none; full paper and supplemental material are present
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests how initialization and depth affect training of plain convolutional networks, using training curves and accuracy outcomes rather than the exact original experiments in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The reported experiments directly measure training or accuracy outcomes. The cited results from prior work are not entered as rows. Figure 1 reports training curves, but the text does not give their training-accuracy values separately.
record.test_reason: The study directly measures training accuracy, learning speed and trainable depth under different initializations in plain tanh CNNs. It tests V1 on clean CIFAR-10 and the special-initialization portions of V3 and V4. It is an original source for V3 and V4, so those versions receive no verdict labels.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors demonstrate training plain CNNs through 10,000 layers using theoretically chosen initialization, report saturation of test performance beyond tens or hundreds of layers, and suggest residual connections and batch normalization also help define a useful model class. The latter interpretation is a suggestion, not a matched architectural comparison.
record.recipe_differences: Uses gradient-based training from random initialization, but specifically evaluates theoretically chosen critical orthogonal and Delta-Orthogonal initialization; experiments use tanh CNNs and include MNIST and CIFAR-10.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization type and spatial variance; depth.

fits_no_version.finding: Spatially uniform orthogonal initialization gives about 70% test accuracy at depth 2048; test performance degrades with depth despite perfect training accuracy. Spatial variance choices also affect generalization in Figure 4.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization's spatial variance structure affects the generalization of very deep CNNs even when they fit the training data.

record.problems: The experiments use tanh and specially tuned initialization; CIFAR-100 and label corruption are not evaluated. Some plotted training outcomes lack separate numerical values in the text. The 4,000-layer accuracy statement does not identify whether the 95% value is training or test accuracy.
record.rows_left_out: No reported experimental result that bears on the tested versions was omitted.

untested.parts: CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, and controlled comparisons involving smaller models, early stopping or regularization. The early-stopped 8192-layer run does not establish substantial residual training error.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student optimization, spurious local minima and extra student neurons.
The plain batch-normalized versus identity-shortcut comparison, longer-training controls, ImageNet and Fixup.
Direct Glorot/He initialization comparisons and orthogonal-versus-Gaussian comparisons in fully connected tanh networks.
Learning rates relative to stability thresholds, catapult dynamics, curvature and edge-of-stability training.
Matched comparisons of training speed or learning-rate tolerance with and without batch normalization, and Fixup.

missing.what: The MNIST training-accuracy sweep over depths 10–600 and initial weight variances 0–4, measured after 500, 2500, 10,000 and 100,000 steps. The authors explicitly report agreement between trainability and the predicted signal-propagation depth scale. Add rows for the initialization-dependent trainability result; exact heatmap accuracies are unavailable in the supplied text.

record.verdict_notes: V3 and V4 verdicts are withheld because this study is an original source for those versions. R2 requires separate rows to represent its observed trainability findings and its unreadable terminal training-accuracy values.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, smaller models, early stopping, and regularized recipes are not tested.
The paper does not compare identity shortcuts with plain networks; it tests whether special initialization permits training plain networks at great depth.
The paper does not test Glorot or He initialization, deep tanh fully connected networks, or 10,000-layer plain convolutional networks with Gaussian kernels.

rows.subject: CNNs initialized critically using orthogonal kernels
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR-10 with spatially uniform orthogonal initialization.
rows.value: 100% training accuracy for all these curves (except for 8192, which was stopped early)
rows.note: The text reports the result across the depth sweep; it does not give separate training-accuracy values for each depth.
rows.check: Restrict the 100% training-accuracy result to depths 32, 128, 512, 2048 and 4096. Figure 3 explicitly excludes the early-stopped 8192-layer run; separate that run rather than assigning it the same outcome.

source_check.locator_found: Figure 3 caption and depth legend; Section 3.3.

rows.subject: CNNs initialized critically using Delta-Orthogonal kernels
rows.operation_detail: Trained on MNIST and CIFAR-10 with Delta-Orthogonal initialization.
rows.value: Figure 1 shows training and test curves; numerical training accuracy is not stated in the text.
rows.note: The authors state that all these networks learn quickly and that learning time in epochs is independent of depth; the numeric training outcomes appear only in curves.
rows.check: Split by dataset and outcome. Only CIFAR-10 bears on V1, whose near-zero training-error outcome cannot be read from the supplied figure text. For V3 and V4, successful training through 10,000 layers and depth-independent learning time are explicitly observed in Section 3.4; numerical terminal training accuracy is unnecessary to establish those findings.

source_check.correct: Split by dataset and version: V1 cannot_determine for CIFAR-10; MNIST does not test V1. V3 and V4 observed for successful training through 10,000 layers under critical Delta-Orthogonal initialization. Exact training-accuracy endpoints are not stated, but successful training and depth-independent learning time are stated explicitly.
source_check.problem: A single cannot_determine state incorrectly hides the explicit qualitative trainability results bearing on V3 and V4.

rows.subject: 4,000-layer CNN with orthogonal initialization
rows.operation_detail: Trained on MNIST using orthogonal initialization.
rows.value: achieves 95% after 10,000 steps or about 7 epochs
rows.note: The text's wording does not specify whether this 95% is training or test accuracy.
rows.check: The outcome is test accuracy: the sentence reports test accuracy above 60% after one epoch and continues to 95% after about seven epochs. Together with R4, this establishes substantially faster learning with orthogonal initialization; 95% accuracy does not make the initialization-speed effect partial.

rows.subject: 4,000-layer CNN with critically-tuned Gaussian initialization
rows.operation_detail: Trained on MNIST using critically-tuned Gaussian initialization with the same weight variance as the orthogonal initialization.
rows.value: test and training accuracy is below 60% after 90,000 steps, about 60 epochs
rows.note: The text gives a joint bound for test and training accuracy rather than separate values.
rows.check: The below-60% training and test accuracy after 90,000 steps is the Gaussian comparator supporting the orthogonal speed advantage in R3, rather than a partial realization of that advantage.

rows.subject: 2048-layer CNN initialized with spatially uniform orthogonal kernels
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR-10 using spatially uniform orthogonal initialization.
rows.note: The result is a test-accuracy outcome, so it does not establish training error.
rows.check: This isolated test-accuracy result measures generalization, not training speed, trainable depth or training error. It does not establish a V4 limitation.

relationships.condition: Clean CIFAR-10; critically initialized plain tanh CNNs with spatially uniform orthogonal kernels, depths 32–4096.
relationships.reason: R1 reports 100% training accuracy at every completed depth in this group.
relationships.display_finding: Training accuracy reached 100% at every completed depth in the 32–4096 range.
